beats.act: the game and both effects
beats.narration_text: Jelly Hop is Kiran's game: a jelly cube hops across plates on a dinner table while forks stab down from above. Effect A is the landing crumb puff. Its event is player dot just landed, read while the state is PLAYING: the same tick that plays the landing sound. Effect B is the dome's sugar glints. Its job is ambience, and its condition is simply that the state is not WON.

beats.act: emission, process, draw
beats.narration_text: Every particle system has three parts. Emission decides when, and how many, are born: line sixty-nine of the land puff scene sets explosiveness to one, so all sixteen crumbs are born on the landing frame. Process moves each particle, every frame: line three forty-three of the generated process shader starts the force with gravity. Draw decides what each one looks like: line sixty-five gives every crumb its gradient texture.

props.title: Three Parts, One Line Each
props.status: Lines read from the committed files · typeset, not a screenshot

beats.act: why a low headless CPU cost is expected, and what was measured
beats.narration_text: That split predicts the price. On a GPU particles node, the process step is a particles shader that runs on the GPU, and a headless run measures CPU time only, so a low headless CPU cost is expected. What Kiran measured: none of the three effect cases could be distinguished from the effects-off baseline within the observed spread. That is not a measured zero. And the run did not establish what ran on the GPU: its log reports open G L three, and the dummy-renderer statement is still unconfirmed.

props.title: The Headless Price: Expected, Then Measured

beats.act: Effect A: the intent block
beats.narration_text: Kiran wrote Effect A's intent before any scene existed. Three phases, counted in thirty-frames-per-second frames from the landing: impact by frame two, a fast sideways kick to about one jelly width by frame five, and a settle that is gone by frame twelve. Each crumb has a light cream core and a dark brown rim, so it reads on the pale plate and on the dark table. Six to twelve pixels, drawn behind the jelly.

beats.act: code: the LandPuff emitter node
beats.narration_text: The emitter node, written by Claude Code from the brief's table. Amount sixteen. One shot true: one burst, then done. Explosiveness one: all sixteen at once. Emitting is false in the file; the driver turns it on at the landing. And line sixty-five is the draw side: the crumb texture, a gradient defined inside this same file.

beats.act: result: strip r0 and Kiran's verdict
beats.narration_text: The result, as a fixture: Kiran's preview scene with two still jellies, captured by Movie Maker as strip r zero. Kiran's verdict, given before Claude read anything: at frame twelve the puff was easy to see on both the plate and the table. But at frame fifteen most crumbs were still under the jellies, with no wide sideways fan. By frame twenty, gone.

Claude first proposed doubling the push range; Kiran chose this curve-only alternative instead.

beats.act: Effect B: the intent block
beats.narration_text: Effect B's intent. Ambience: about twenty-four glints at a time, each drifting upward over two point four seconds, sugar white turning pale gold. Full from the very first frame, with no fill-in. At the win, no new glints; the live ones rise and fade. And the feature Effect A does not use: a box emission shape across the dome's glass, with an additive draw material.

props.title: Effect B: The Intent, Written First
props.status: Quoted from CHANGE-BRIEF.md · typeset, not a screenshot

beats.act: code: box emission and the additive material
beats.narration_text: Here is the box. Line thirty-four sets the emission shape to three, a box, and line thirty-five makes it seventy by forty-five pixels each way from the centre, so a glint can be born anywhere across the glass. A slight negative gravity drifts them upward. The draw side is additive: line sixteen's canvas item material uses blend mode add, so glints brighten whatever is behind them.

beats.act: two lines of Godot's generated process shader
beats.narration_text: Kiran converted the puff's process material into a shader and saved Godot's output unedited; the game does not use it. Line one forty-five picks each particle's starting speed between the minimum and the maximum, with a seeded random value: the brief's thirty to sixty. Line two fifty-four scales the radial push by the curve, sampled at the particle's lifetime percentage: Kiran's revision one curve, held at one until point one eight, zero by point two.

props.title: The Generated Shader Beside the Brief
props.status: Lines read from the files · typeset, not a screenshot

beats.act: what the tests proved
beats.narration_text: What the tests proved, each run by Kiran at sixty frames per second. The two config tests read every setting back: fifty-one checks and forty-five, no failures. The Effect A state test, twenty-four checks: one puff per landing sound, on the same tick, at the feet to zero point zero pixels. The Effect B state test, twenty-seven: emitting equals not WON on all sixteen hundred sixty-seven ticks.

props.title: What the Tests Proved
props.status: Logs of runs by Kiran · headless · numbers only, not a render

beats.act: two mutations that failed the config test
beats.narration_text: Two mutations, each a one-line edit that Kiran made and then restored. A Godot three name, initial velocity instead of initial velocity min: Godot printed nothing, the puff still fired in the preview, and the config test failed, reading zero instead of thirty. Then spread changed to forty-five while the brief still said thirty: exactly one failure. A firing puff was not proof that its settings had loaded.

props.title: Two Mutations the Config Test Caught
props.status: Logs of runs by Kiran · each exited 1

beats.act: both prices against the budgets
beats.narration_text: Both prices, against the budgets. Headless CPU: unresolved, every effect inside the run-to-run spread. GPU: the brief's budget is a quarter of a millisecond per effect. On the shipped Compatibility renderer the Visual Profiler showed CPU timings, but every GPU reading was zero point zero and the graph was blank. A labelled Forward-plus comparison did the same. So GPU timing was unavailable, and both budgets are unverified.

props.title: The Prices Against the Budgets
props.status: Kiran's Visual Profiler screenshots · Apple M4

beats.act: what no headless run can show
beats.narration_text: And what no headless run can show: that a crumb or a glint is drawn at all; the timing phases, the scale, the contrast and the variation; whether two puffs' crumbs visibly overlap; a pop at the screen edge; or whether restart refills the dome. Those are checks for eyes on the running game, and several are still open.

beats.act: verdict
beats.narration_text: Verdict. Both effects fire where the brief says: one puff per landing sound, glints off exactly while WON, with fifty-one, forty-five, twenty-four and twenty-seven checks and no failures. The prices are unresolved: CPU inside the spread, GPU timing unavailable, both budgets unverified. Kiran wrote the brief and both revisions, made every verdict, ran every test, mutation and profiler run, and started all four strip captures. Claude Code built the effect scenes, the driver, the tests and the cost script, and made this film; Claude in chat drafted the brief's wording and wrote the peak checker. The textures are two gradient textures defined in the scene files: no third-party textures. Kiran's next step, in Kiran's words: I'd check whether the dome glints are already full immediately after an in-game replay. The preview showed full glints by frame 10, but I haven't checked that in live play. Shown at revision eight zero zero four D E A.

beats.act: your turn handoff
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Use Walker: before tuning a particle effect, write what frames 2, 5 and 12 should show, capture a fixed-seed strip, predict exactly what one setting change will move, capture again, and tell me which frame proved my prediction wrong. Writing frames first is what let Kiran see crumbs stuck under the jelly at frame fifteen, and what showed that Claude's own prediction was one frame off. Run it on your own effect, and watch which frame surprises you. Liam, in for Bear.
